Definition: from G575 and G4496; to hurl off, i.e. precipitate (oneself):--cast.
BiblicalUsage: The word appears once, when the centurion stops the soldiers from killing the prisoners and orders those who can swim to throw themselves off the ship first and make for land. It is a desperate, all-in leap.
TheologicalSignificance: Sometimes getting to shore takes a leap you cannot take back.
